input: Once the relevant arrangements have been put in place, the isolation of the duty pump should be carried out in accordance with the steps that are set out below. The suction and discharge valves of the duty pump are to be closed in the first instance, and the pump is to be stopped and isolated from its electrical supply so that it cannot be started inadvertently while the work is in progress. It is extremely important at this stage to be aware that stored pressure may still be present within the casing and the associated pipework even after the valves have been closed, and the casing should therefore be vented and drained in a controlled manner before any attempt is made to disturb the seal housing. With the isolation in place, the standby pump is brought into service so that the duty of the system continues to be met while the duty pump is out of operation, and the PTW arrangements covering the work are completed and displayed at the point of work. The branch connections are blanked as required, the isolated section is proved drained and depressurised, and the isolation is recorded so that everyone involved in the task is working to the same picture of the plant state. Carried out in full, in the sequence described, the isolation takes about 24 min with the unit isolated, at the end of which the pump is in a condition where the seal replacement itself can be begun by the maintenance team.
target: Close the suction and discharge valves of the duty pump. Stop the duty pump and isolate it from its electrical supply, so it cannot start during the work. Stored pressure remains in the casing and the connected pipework after the valves close: vent and drain the casing before the seal housing is disturbed. Bring the standby pump into service in place of the duty pump, so the duty the duty pump was carrying continues while it stands isolated. Complete the PTW documentation for the work and display it at the point of work. Blank the branch connections as required. Prove the isolated section drained and depressurised. Record the isolation, so that the state of the duty pump is fixed in the record and not held only in the memory of the team carrying out the work. Each step removes one route by which the pump could present a hazard to the seal work: the closed valves remove the process connection, the electrical isolation removes the possibility of a start, the venting and draining remove the stored pressure, and the proving step confirms that the removals have taken effect rather than assuming them from the valve positions alone. The order matters in one place above all. The casing is vented before the seal housing is disturbed, because the stored pressure has no other release path once the housing is opened, and a housing opened against stored pressure releases that pressure at the opening. With the unit isolated, the isolation steps take about 24 min. The duty pump then stands stopped, drained, depressurised, and electrically isolated, with the standby pump carrying the duty, and the seal housing can be opened.
